fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Steep Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow fire and emergency apparatus to reach the structure without obstruction.
• Clear a turnaround area near the residence large enough for an emergency vehicle to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive so that branches do not block the roof line of a full-size emergency vehicle.
• Cut back dense vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clear sightlines for approaching responders.
• Remove or thin vegetation growing directly against the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around the buildings on foot.
• Trim vegetation along the walkway connecting the main residence to the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings quickly.
• Mark any steep grade changes along the access drive or walkway with reflective stakes or markers to alert responders arriving at night or in low visibility.
• Keep perimeter fence gates unlocked or fitted with a knox-box or standardized lock so responders can pass through without delay.
• Identify and mark the gate or fence opening nearest the detached structure so responders can locate it quickly under emergency conditions.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Mixed Vegetation; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Woody Debris; Large Trees
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees and shrubs on all sides of the structure to create open space between the vegetation and the walls.
• Remove woody debris, brush piles, and dead plant material from around the base of the structure.
• Trim lower branches on large trees near the structure so the lowest branches are well above the ground.
• Separate shrubs from each other and from the structure so there are clear gaps between them.
• Clear ground vegetation growing directly against the foundation and exterior walls.
• Thin the tree cluster near the structure so individual trees are spaced apart with open ground between them.
• Remove dead branches and dead material from within the scattered trees near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and debris along its full length.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate under low visibility conditions.
• Remove any woody debris piles stored near or under large trees close to the structure.
• Thin mixed shrub and tree vegetation on the uphill or dominant wind-exposed sides of the structure first.
• Keep a clear, open path around the perimeter of the structure so a person can walk freely around all sides.
